name: Kit Salcedo
life: Kit rented the shoeshine stool after losing a restaurant job. He makes enough on hearing days to skip the humiliating half-shift his old manager still offers him. People tipping too generously put that pride in a difficult place. On Sunday, near Studio Boulevard, Kit waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I gave the borrowed shoes a polish on the bank steps. He kept offering me a note. I finally took it because he was starting to feel like everybody's charity case.
appearance: Kit is easy to recognize by a center part and straight chestnut hair and a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Usually dressed in a soft blue checked shirt with a replacement button a shade darker than the others, Kit gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Kit is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Kit loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To earn enough on ordinary paid shines to keep the stool on the bank steps.
family: Shay Lloyd is Kit’s older cousin. A parent had a second job that nobody mentioned at school. Years later the family discovered two sets of friends who thought they knew entirely different people. Kit can usually spot the person covering a double shift. Asked about *The second dog*, Shay says, “I fostered both litters. Their ears fold the same way until somebody says dinner.”
connections: Alma Faye. One finishes the borrowed shoes while the other frames the cuff that won't match them.
